raw_text:
Here’s a 12-week strength program starting 2026-06-01 designed for an advanced lifter in early perimenopause, prioritizing bone-loading compound lifts, heat management, and recovery. It uses a 3-days-on/1-day-off cadence within the week where appropriate and emphasizes heavy axial loading, multi-planar compound work, and progressive overload while respecting heat intolerance. Assume 4 strength days per week plus one optional short power/plyo technique session. Deloads built in. All sessions planned in cooler times of day if possible.

Global structure
- Frequency: 4 strength sessions/week (Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat suggested). Optional 30–40 min neural/power technique on Wed in cooler environment.
- Phases:
  1) Weeks 1–3 Foundation and Heat Acclimatized Strength
  2) Weeks 4–6 Intensification (Strength Emphasis)
  3) Weeks 7–9 Peak Bone-Loading + Power Emphasis
  4) Weeks 10–12 Consolidation + Deload + Rebuild
- Primary lifts: Back squat/front squat, deadlift/hex-bar DL, bench press, overhead press, weighted pull-ups/rows, hip thrusts, split squats, carries, Olympic-derivative pulls (from blocks), step-downs, jump landings.
- Bone loading strategy: High strain magnitude and rate via heavy axial lifts (3–5 reps), impact landings (low volume, high quality), loaded carries, multidirectional lower-body work. Short contact, firm landings, manage volume to avoid overheating.
- Progression: Double progression within rep ranges; increase load 2–2.5% weekly where bar speed and RPE allow. Use RPE caps and bar speed cutoffs.
- Heat management: Session timing in cool hours; pre-cooling and post-cooling protocols included below.

General session template (for all weeks)
- Pre-cooling (10–15 min): 500 ml cold water with electrolytes over 10 min; cool neck wrap or forearm cold-pack immersion 8–10 min; breathable clothing.
- Warm-up (10–15 min): 
  - 5 min easy cyc/row/fan bike in cool setting
  - Mobility: T-spine extension/rotation x6 each, ankle rocks x10, 90/90 hip x6/side
  - Activation: mini-band lateral walks 2x12, glute bridge 2x10, scap push-up 2x10
  - Movement prep: 2–3 ramp sets of first lift (50/65/80%)
- Main lifts: As per week plan. Use fans and shaded/cool room; rest 2–3 min on secondary; 3–5 min on main sets.
- Intra-session cooling: Cold towel/ice slushie sips between heavy sets; pause if HR or heat symptoms spike; cap session to 70–80 min.
- Post-session cooling (10–12 min): Forearm immersion 12–18°C for 8–10 min or cool shower; cold beverage with electrolytes; light stretch.
- RPE guide: Main lifts RPE 7–9 (no grinders to failure). Stop set when bar speed drops >20% of first work set.
- Plyo safety: Low volume, high intent, long rest, land softly with good mechanics, stop if heat symptoms rise.

Nutrition, hydration, recovery
- Daily protein 1.8–2.2 g/kg; distribute 4 servings (0.4–0.55 g/kg per meal) with 2–3 g leucine per feeding.
- Carbs 3–5 g/kg non-heavy days; 4–6 g/kg heavy days; include 30–45 g carb + 20–30 g protein 60–90 min pre and within 60 min post.
- Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day; Vitamin D3 1000–2000 IU/day if needed; calcium 1000–1200 mg/day via food/supps; omega-3 1–2 g EPA+DHA/day.
- Hydration: 6–8 ml/kg in the 2 hours pre; 3–5 ml/kg during as tolerated; add 500–700 mg sodium/L in heat.
- Sleep: 7.5–9 h; cool bedroom; reduce alcohol hot-flash triggers; consider magnesium glycinate 200–300 mg in evening if tolerated.
- Symptom-aware autoregulation: If hot flashes/night sweats severe, drop top set intensity by ~2.5–5% or reduce one accessory and extend rest.

Key weekly layout
- Day 1: Lower A (Squat emphasis + impact)
- Day 2: Upper A (Bench emphasis + vertical pull)
- Day 3: Optional Power/Technique (short, cool environment) OR mobility/conditioning
- Day 4: Lower B (Hinge emphasis + unilateral)
- Day 5: Upper B (Press/Row + carries)

Phase 1: Weeks 1–3 Foundation and Heat-Aware Strength
Goal: Groove heavy patterns, moderate volume, introduce low-dose impact and carries. RPE 7–8.

Week 1 (2026-06-01 start)
- Day 1 Lower A
  - Back squat 4x5 @70–75% (RPE 7–8)
  - Paused back squat 2x3 @65%
  - Step-downs (box, controlled) 3x6/side
  - Hip thrust 3x8
  - Low pogo hops 3x10 (sub if heat spikes)
  - Farmer carry heavy 4x30 m
- Day 2 Upper A
  - Bench press 4x5 @70–75%
  - Incline DB press 3x8
  - Weighted pull-up 4x4–6
  - One-arm cable row 3x10/side
  - Face pulls 3x12–15
- Day 3 Optional Power
  - Hang high pull from blocks 5x3 @50–60%, full rest
  - Box jump step-downs 3x3
  - Med ball chest pass 4x5
- Day 4 Lower B
  - Trap bar deadlift 4x4 @75% (RPE 7–8)
  - Romanian deadlift 3x6
  - Front-foot elevated split squat 3x8/side
  - Tib raises 3x15; calf raises 3x12
- Day 5 Upper B
  - Overhead press 4x4–5 @70–75%
  - Close-grip bench 3x6
  - Chest-supported row 4x6–8
  - Lat pulldown neutral 3x8–10
  - Suitcase carry 3x30 m/side

Week 2
- Slight load increase 2–2.5% if RPE ≤8; maintain volumes.
- Lower A
  - Back squat 5x4 @75–77.5%
  - Pause squat 2x3 @67.5%
  - Lateral lunge 3x6/side
  - Hip thrust 3x8
  - Pogo hops 3x12
  - Farmer carry 4x30–40 m
- Upper A
  - Bench 5x4 @75–77.5%
  - DB incline 3x8
  - Weighted pull-up 4x4–6
  - One-arm row 3x10/side
  - Face pulls 3x15
- Optional Power
  - Clean pull from blocks 5x3 @60%
  - Seated MB overhead throw 4x5
- Lower B
  - Conventional deadlift 4x4 @75–80%
  - RDL 3x6
  - Bulgarian split squat 3x8/side
  - Tib/calf 3x12–15
- Upper B
  - OHP 5x3–4 @75–80%
  - Weighted dip 3x6–8
  - Chest-supported row 4x6–8
  - Lat pulldown 3x8–10
  - Suitcase carry 4x30 m

Week 3
- Aim top sets RPE 8.5; do not grind.
- Lower A
  - Back squat 5x3 @80%
  - Pause squat 2x2 @70%
  - Step-downs 3x6/side
  - Hip thrust 3x6–8 (heavier)
  - Low depth jumps (12–18") 3x3 or substitute pogos
  - Farmer carry 5x30–40 m
- Upper A
  - Bench 5x3 @80%
  - Incline DB 3x6–8
  - Weighted pull-up 5x3–5
  - One-arm row 3x8–10
  - Band external rotation 3x15
- Optional Power
  - High pulls 5x2 @60–65%
  - MB rotational throw 4x4/side
- Lower B
  - Deadlift 5x3 @80%
  - RDL 3x5–6
  - Split squat 3x6–8/side
  - Tib/calf 3x12–15
- Upper B
  - OHP 5x3 @80%
  - Close-grip bench 3x5–6
  - Row 4x6–8
  - Pulldown 3x8–10
  - Suitcase carry 4x40 m

Phase 2: Weeks 4–6 Intensification (Strength Emphasis)
Goal: Raise intensity, reduce accessory volume slightly, maintain impact dose. RPE peaks ~8.5–9 sparingly.

Week 4
- Lower A
  - Back squat 1 top set 3 @85%, then 3x3 @80%
  - Front squat 3x3 @72–75%
  - Step-downs 3x5/side
  - Hip thrust 3x5–6 heavy
  - Depth jumps 3x3 (or pogos)
  - Farmer carry 4x40 m
- Upper A
  - Bench 1x3 @85%, then 3x3 @80%
  - Larsen press 3x4–5
  - Weighted pull-up 4x3–5
  - Chest-supported row 3x6–8
- Optional Power
  - Clean pulls from blocks 6x2 @70%
  - MB chest pass 4x4
- Lower B
  - Deadlift 1x3 @85%, then 3x3 @80%
  - RDL 3x5
  - Bulgarian split squat 3x6/side
- Upper B
  - OHP 1x3 @85%, then 3x3 @80%
  - Close-grip bench 3x4–5
  - Row 4x5–6
  - Suitcase carry 4x40–50 m

Week 5
- Slight load bump if barspeed good.
- Lower A: Back squat 4x2 @87–88%; Front squat 3x2 @77%
- Upper A: Bench 4x2 @87–88%; Weighted pull-up 5x2–4
- Optional Power: High pull 6x2 @70–75%; MB rotational throw 4x3/side
- Lower B: Deadlift 4x2 @87–88%; RDL 3x4–5; Split squat 3x5/side
- Upper B: OHP 4x2 @85%; Row 4x5–6; Dips 3x5–6; Carries 4x50 m

Week 6 (deload-ish on accessories, hold intensity brief)
- Lower A: Back squat 3x2 @85%; Front squat 2x3 @70%; Hip thrust 2x6; Pogo 2x10; Carries 3x30 m
- Upper A: Bench 3x2 @85%; Pull-up 3x3; Row 2x8
- Optional Power: Technique only, 20–25 min
- Lower B: Deadlift 3x2 @85%; Split squat 2x6; Tib/calf 2x12
- Upper B: OHP 3x2 @82–85%; Pulldown 2x8; Face pulls 2x12

Phase 3: Weeks 7–9 Peak Bone-Loading + Power
Goal: Heaviest axial loading with low rep sets; maintain short impact work; integrate loaded jumps where tolerated. Keep sessions tightly managed for heat.

Week 7
- Lower A
  - Back squat 5x2 @88–90% (RPE ≤8.5)
  - Front squat 3x2 @78–80%
  - Depth jumps 3x2
  - Farmer carry heavy 5x40 m
- Upper A
  - Bench 5x2 @88–90%
  - Weighted pull-up 5x2–3 (slight load up)
  - Row 3x5–6
- Optional Power
  - Clean pulls 5x2 @75–80%
  - MB overhead throw 4x3
- Lower B
  - Deadlift 5x2 @88–90%
  - RDL 3x3–4
  - Bulgarian split squat 3x5/side
- Upper B
  - OHP 5x2 @87–90%
  - Close-grip bench 3x3–4
  - Suitcase carry 4x50–60 m

Week 8
- If recovery good: introduce single top set.
- Lower A: Back squat 1x1 @92% (no grind), then 3x2 @88%; Front squat 3x2 @80%; Depth jumps 3x2; Carries 4x50–60 m
- Upper A: Bench 1x1 @92%, then 3x2 @88%; Weighted pull-up 4x2–3; Row 3x5
- Optional Power: High pull 5x2 @75–80%; MB rotational 4x3/side
- Lower B: Deadlift 1x1 @92%, then 3x2 @88%; RDL 3x3; Split squat 3x5/side
- Upper B: OHP 1x1 @90–92%, then 3x2 @87%; Rows 3x5; Dips 3x4–5; Carries 4x60 m

Week 9 (taper intensity slightly, maintain power)
- Lower A: Back squat 4x2 @86–88%; Front squat 2x2 @75%; Pogo 3x12; Carries 3x50 m
- Upper A: Bench 4x2 @86–88%; Pull-up 4x2–3; Row 3x6
- Optional Power: Technique 20 min, low fatigue
- Lower B: Deadlift 4x2 @86–88%; Split squat 2x5/side
- Upper B: OHP 4x2 @85–87%; Pulldown 3x8; Face pulls 2x12

Phase 4: Weeks 10–12 Consolidation + Deload + Rebuild
Goal: Reduce cumulative fatigue, maintain strength, re-expand volume slightly with moderate intensities, set up next cycle.

Week 10 (Deload)
- Keep heat very low; shorten sessions 45–60 min.
- Lower A: Back squat 3x3 @72–75%; Step-downs 2x6; Carries 2x30 m
- Upper A: Bench 3x3 @72–75%; Pull-up BW 3x4; Row 2x8
- Optional: Skip or mobility only
- Lower B: Trap bar deadlift 3x3 @72–75%; Split squat 2x6
- Upper B: OHP 3x3 @70–72%; Pulldown 2x8–10; Band work 2x15

Week 11 (Rebuild volume at moderate load)
- Lower A
  - Back squat 4x4 @77–80%
  - Front squat 3x3 @72–75%
  - Lateral lunge 3x6/side
  - Hip thrust 3x8
  - Pogo 3x12
  - Farmer carry 3x40–50 m
- Upper A
  - Bench 4x4 @77–80%
  - Incline DB 3x8
  - Weighted pull-up 4x4–5
  - Row 3x8
- Optional Power: High pull 4x3 @65–70%; MB throw 3x4
- Lower B
  - Deadlift 4x3 @80%
  - RDL 3x5
  - Bulgarian split squat 3x6/side
- Upper B
  - OHP 4x4 @75–77%
  - Close-grip bench 3x5–6
  - Suitcase carry 3x50–60 m

Week 12 (Consolidate and test submax strength)
- Lower A
  - Back squat 1x2 @85%, 2x2 @82%; optional rep PR at 80% AMRAP cap RPE 8
  - Front squat 3x2 @75%
  - Depth jump or pogo 3x10–12
  - Farmer carry 4x50 m
- Upper A
  - Bench 1x2 @85%, 2x2 @82%; optional AMRAP at 80% cap RPE 8
  - Weighted pull-up 4x3–4
  - Row 3x6–8
- Optional Power: Technique or skip
- Lower B
  - Deadlift 1x2 @85%, 2x2 @82%; optional AMRAP 80% cap RPE 8
  - RDL 2x4
  - Split squat 2x6/side
- Upper B
  - OHP 1x2 @85%, 2x2 @80–82%
  - Dips 3x4–6
  - Suitcase carry 4x50–60 m

Conditioning (optional, low heat load)
- 1–2x/week 20–25 min low-to-moderate effort in cool environment (fan bike/rower), HR 60–70% max, finish with 5 min cool-down.
- Avoid fasted high-intensity and hot environments per restriction.

Menstrual/perimenopause considerations
- Cycle irregularity means plan by symptoms rather than dates:
  - Hot-flash clusters or severe night sweats: choose “B option” that day: drop the top set, shorten accessories, extend rest, or swap to trap-bar variation to reduce CNS/axial stress.
  - If spotting or poor sleep: cap RPE at 7–8; switch impact to pogos or skip.
  - If a strong-feel day: take the planned top single/double within RPE cap, not beyond.

Monitoring and progression notes
- Keep a bar-speed or RPE log. If two consecutive sessions hit RPE 9 early or heat symptoms interrupt, reduce next week’s intensities by 2.5% and trim one accessory.
- If all main lifts feel ≤RPE 8 across a week, add 2–2.5% the following week or add one back-off set.
- Technique priority: neutral spine under axial load; strict depth/tempo on step-downs for patellar tendon/bone stimulus.

Equipment/environment tips
- Train with fans, open door, or air-conditioned space.
- Use chalk (dry hands reduce perceived heat).
- Cooling towels/ice slurry available each session.
- Breathable, light-colored clothing; avoid infrared heaters or sunlit platforms.

This plan maintains high bone-relevant strain via heavy squats/deadlifts, periodic impact, and carries, while embedding heat-safe protocols and autoregulation for perimenopausal symptoms. Adjust set counts or swap trap bar/box squat variants on warmer days while preserving the main weekly intensity targets.
